questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which observation is best explained by cohesion between water molecules?
options: Water can be pulled up xylem vessels under tension
questions.answer: Water can be pulled up xylem vessels under tension
questions.hint: Cohesion is attraction between molecules of the same substance.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which polysaccharide has β-1,4 glycosidic bonds that produce straight chains linked by hydrogen bonds?
questions.hint: It is a structural polysaccharide in plant cell walls.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which level of protein structure is stabilised by interactions between R-groups, such as disulfide bridges and ionic bonds?
questions.hint: It describes the overall three-dimensional folding of a single polypeptide.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which statement describes a saturated fatty acid?
options: It always has a cis double bond
It is always liquid at room temperature
It has no carbon–carbon double bonds
It has one carbon–carbon double bond
questions.answer: It has no carbon–carbon double bonds
questions.hint: Saturated means every carbon holds as many hydrogens as possible.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: What does it mean that the two strands of DNA are antiparallel?
options: They run in opposite directions, one 5′→3′ and the other 3′→5′
They run in the same direction
questions.answer: They run in opposite directions, one 5′→3′ and the other 3′→5′
questions.hint: Think about the orientation of the sugar-phosphate backbones.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: An enzyme-catalysed reaction releases 12 cm³ of oxygen in 4 minutes. Calculate the mean rate in cm³ min⁻¹.
questions.hint: Rate = amount of product ÷ time.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: What is the effect of a non-competitive inhibitor on an enzyme-catalysed reaction?
options: Its effect disappears at high substrate concentration
It lowers Vmax, and increasing substrate concentration cannot overcome it
It has no effect on Vmax
questions.answer: It lowers Vmax, and increasing substrate concentration cannot overcome it
questions.hint: It binds away from the active site and changes its shape.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: In end-product inhibition of a metabolic pathway, where does the end product bind?
options: to the DNA coding for the enzyme
to the active site of the last enzyme in the pathway
to the substrate of the first reaction
to an allosteric site on an enzyme early in the pathway
questions.answer: to an allosteric site on an enzyme early in the pathway
questions.hint: The aim is to stop the whole pathway at its start.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Name the type of nuclear division that produces four genetically different haploid nuclei.
questions.hint: It involves two divisions and crossing over.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which observation supports the endosymbiotic theory for the origin of mitochondria?
options: Mitochondria have their own 70S ribosomes and circular DNA
Mitochondria are produced by the Golgi apparatus
Mitochondria have a cell wall made of cellulose
Mitochondria are found in all prokaryotes
questions.answer: Mitochondria have their own 70S ribosomes and circular DNA
questions.hint: Compare mitochondria with bacteria.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Experiments with sterilised broth in swan-necked flasks provided evidence against which idea?
questions.hint: Microorganisms only appeared when the neck was broken.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which molecule is thought to have been both a store of genetic information and a catalyst in the earliest cells?
questions.hint: Some forms of this molecule act as ribozymes.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Name the enzyme that retroviruses use to make DNA from an RNA template.
questions.hint: Its name describes the opposite of normal transcription.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which feature is shared by all viruses?
options: genetic material enclosed in a protein capsid
questions.answer: genetic material enclosed in a protein capsid
questions.hint: Viruses lack the structures needed for their own metabolism.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: What happens at the end of the lytic cycle of a bacteriophage?
options: The host cell bursts and releases new virus particles
The host cell divides normally for many generations
Viral DNA integrates into the host chromosome
questions.answer: The host cell bursts and releases new virus particles
questions.hint: Lysis means splitting.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Discuss whether viruses should be classified as living organisms.
questions.hint: Compare viruses with the functions of life and with cell theory, then reach a conclusion.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which type of bond forms between neighbouring water molecules?
questions.hint: Think of the attraction between the slightly positive H of one molecule and the slightly negative O of another.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Name the monomer that is joined to form starch and glycogen.
questions.hint: It is a hexose monosaccharide.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which type of reaction joins two monosaccharides to form a disaccharide?
questions.hint: A water molecule is released.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Why do phospholipids form a bilayer in water?
options: They form peptide bonds with water
They have hydrophilic phosphate heads and hydrophobic hydrocarbon tails
questions.answer: They have hydrophilic phosphate heads and hydrophobic hydrocarbon tails
questions.hint: Consider which part of the molecule is attracted to water.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Name the bond that links amino acids in a polypeptide.
questions.hint: It forms between the amine group of one amino acid and the carboxyl group of another.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which nitrogenous base is found in RNA but not in DNA?
questions.hint: In RNA it pairs with adenine.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: A DNA sample contains 22% adenine. What percentage of its bases are cytosine?
questions.hint: Use complementary base pairing: A = T and C = G, and all bases add up to 100%.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Explain what happens to an enzyme at temperatures well above its optimum.
options: The enzyme is used up in the reaction
The substrate becomes denatured but the enzyme is unchanged
Bonds holding its shape break, the active site changes and the substrate can no longer bind
Molecules move more slowly and collide less
questions.answer: Bonds holding its shape break, the active site changes and the substrate can no longer bind
questions.hint: Think about the tertiary structure of the protein.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which statement describes competitive inhibition?
options: The inhibitor permanently destroys the enzyme’s primary structure
The inhibitor increases the rate of the reaction
The inhibitor binds to a site away from the active site
The inhibitor has a similar shape to the substrate and binds to the active site
questions.answer: The inhibitor has a similar shape to the substrate and binds to the active site
questions.hint: Competition is for the same place on the enzyme.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: A drawing of a mitochondrion is 30 mm long. The actual length is 15 μm. Calculate the magnification.
questions.hint: Convert both lengths to the same unit, then use image size ÷ actual size.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which structure is found in prokaryotic cells?
options: a nucleus with a nuclear membrane
questions.hint: Prokaryotes lack membrane-bound organelles.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Name the passive movement of water across a partially permeable membrane towards a higher solute concentration.
questions.hint: It does not require energy from ATP.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which type of membrane transport requires energy from ATP?
questions.hint: Look for movement against a concentration gradient.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: In which phase of mitosis do sister chromatids separate and move to opposite poles?
questions.hint: It comes straight after the chromosomes line up at the equator.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: In a root tip sample of 400 cells, 32 are in mitosis. Calculate the mitotic index as a percentage.
questions.hint: Divide the cells in mitosis by the total number of cells.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Explain how the properties of water allow sweating to cool the body.
questions.hint: Think about hydrogen bonds and the energy needed to change state.

bus-hl.topic: Term 1 review: introduction to business and human resources

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which business activity belongs to the tertiary sector?
questions.hint: This sector provides services.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which activity is the best example of the quaternary sector?
questions.hint: This sector is knowledge-based.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: A new data protection law forces an online retailer to change how it stores customer information. In a STEEPLE analysis this is a:
questions.hint: Ask what kind of external change caused it.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: In a SWOT analysis, a large competitor opening nearby would be classified as:
questions.hint: It is external and potentially harmful.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which Ansoff strategy involves selling more of existing products in existing markets?
questions.hint: It is the lowest-risk quadrant.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which is a typical example of stakeholder conflict?
options: Suppliers want to be paid on time
Shareholders want higher dividends while employees want higher wages
Customers and shareholders both want the firm to survive
questions.answer: Shareholders want higher dividends while employees want higher wages
questions.hint: Look for two groups whose aims compete for the same resources.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: A supermarket chain gets lower unit costs by ordering in very large quantities. This is an example of:
questions.hint: Think about bulk buying.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: A firm had an average workforce of 70 and 14 employees left during the year. Calculate the labour turnover rate (%).
questions.hint: Leavers ÷ average workforce × 100.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: What is delayering?
options: Adding new layers of middle management
Removing one or more levels of hierarchy from an organisation
Reducing the number of products sold
questions.answer: Removing one or more levels of hierarchy from an organisation
questions.hint: Think of the shape of the organisation chart.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which leadership style involves the leader making decisions without consulting employees?
questions.hint: Power is concentrated in one person.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: When two firms with very different values and ways of working merge, the resulting problems are known as:
questions.hint: It relates to organisational culture.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Name the form of industrial action in which employees collectively stop working.
questions.hint: It is the most extreme form of collective action.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: What is meant by a “work-to-rule”?
options: Managers lock employees out of the workplace
Employees do only the minimum required by their contracts
questions.answer: Employees do only the minimum required by their contracts
questions.hint: Rules are followed exactly, and nothing more.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which is an example of a non-financial reward?
questions.hint: It does not involve money.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: What does the IB command term “discuss” require?
options: The precise meaning of a term
A considered and balanced review including a range of arguments, ending with a conclusion
questions.answer: A considered and balanced review including a range of arguments, ending with a conclusion
questions.hint: It is typical of 10-mark questions.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Explain how a culture clash after a merger could affect employee motivation. [4]
questions.hint: Consider values, ways of working and how staff feel about change.

bus-sl.topic: Term 1 review: introduction to business and human resources

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: In which sector of the economy does manufacturing take place?
questions.hint: It involves turning raw materials into finished goods.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which business activity belongs to the primary sector?
questions.hint: This sector extracts natural resources.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: In a SWOT analysis, what does the letter T stand for?
questions.hint: It is an external factor that could harm the business.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which elements of a SWOT analysis are internal to the business?
questions.hint: Internal factors are under the firm’s control.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the factors in a STEEPLE analysis?
questions.hint: List the seven letters and what each represents.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: According to the Ansoff matrix, selling existing products in new markets is called:
questions.hint: The product stays the same; the customers change.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which Ansoff strategy usually carries the highest risk?
questions.hint: It combines two unknowns.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which Ansoff strategy involves launching new products in existing markets?
questions.hint: The customers stay the same.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which of these is an internal stakeholder?
questions.hint: Internal stakeholders are members of the organisation.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which feature describes a privately held company?
options: It is owned by the government
Owners have limited liability and shares are not sold to the general public
Shares are traded on the stock exchange
questions.answer: Owners have limited liability and shares are not sold to the general public
questions.hint: Think about who can buy the shares.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: What is the main aim of a social enterprise?
options: To be run by the government
To achieve social or environmental goals, reinvesting most of its surplus
questions.answer: To achieve social or environmental goals, reinvesting most of its surplus
questions.hint: Profit is a means, not the end.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: In motivation theory, which of these is a hygiene factor rather than a motivator?
questions.hint: Hygiene factors prevent dissatisfaction but do not motivate on their own.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: What is the likely effect of widening managers’ spans of control?
options: A taller structure with more levels
A flatter organisational structure with fewer levels of hierarchy
questions.answer: A flatter organisational structure with fewer levels of hierarchy
questions.hint: Each manager now supervises more people.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: A business employed an average of 80 workers last year and 12 left. Calculate the labour turnover rate (%).
questions.hint: Divide the number who left by the average number employed, then multiply by 100.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: What does the IB command term “define” require?
options: Break down to bring out the essential elements
Give the precise meaning of a word, phrase or concept
Give a balanced review with a conclusion
Give a detailed account including reasons
questions.answer: Give the precise meaning of a word, phrase or concept
questions.hint: It is usually worth 2 marks.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Explain two advantages of a flat organisational structure for a small business. [4]
questions.hint: Think about communication and the cost of management.

chem-hl.topic: Review: atomic structure, the mole and bonding

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Which subatomic particle determines the identity of an element?
questions.hint: Think about what the atomic number counts.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: State the type of bonding present in solid sodium chloride.
questions.hint: Consider a metal combined with a non-metal.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Which is the ground-state electron configuration of chromium (Z = 24)?
questions.hint: Chromium is an exception: a half-filled sub-level gives extra stability.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Chlorine consists of 75.78% chlorine-35 (mass 34.97) and 24.22% chlorine-37 (mass 36.97). Calculate the relative atomic mass of chlorine to 2 decimal places.
questions.hint: Multiply each isotopic mass by its fractional abundance and add.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Calculate the amount, in mol, of water in 9.00 g of H₂O (Mr = 18.02). Give your answer to 3 significant figures.
questions.hint: Use n = m / M.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Methane burns completely: CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O. Calculate the mass, in g, of CO₂ (Mr = 44.01) formed from 0.250 mol of CH₄. Give your answer to 3 significant figures.
questions.hint: Use the mole ratio of CH₄ to CO₂ first.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: For 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O, 4.0 mol of H₂ react with 3.0 mol of O₂. Determine the maximum amount, in mol, of water formed.
questions.hint: Identify the limiting reactant before using the ratio.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Calculate the concentration, in mol dm⁻³, of a solution containing 0.0500 mol of NaOH in 250 cm³ of solution.
questions.hint: Convert the volume to dm³ first.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Calculate the volume, in dm³, occupied by 0.200 mol of an ideal gas at STP (molar volume 22.7 dm³ mol⁻¹). Give your answer to 3 significant figures.
questions.hint: Multiply the amount by the molar volume.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: What is the shape of an ammonia (NH₃) molecule?
questions.hint: Count the bonding pairs and the lone pair around nitrogen.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: What is the hybridisation of each carbon atom in ethene, C₂H₄?
questions.hint: Each carbon has three electron domains.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: How many sigma (σ) and pi (π) bonds are in ethyne, C₂H₂?
questions.hint: A triple bond contains one σ bond; each single bond is one σ bond.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Which explains why the first ionisation energy of oxygen is lower than that of nitrogen?
options: Repulsion between paired electrons in a 2p orbital
Oxygen has a smaller nuclear charge
The electron is removed from a 2s orbital in oxygen
Oxygen has an extra inner shell of electrons
questions.answer: Repulsion between paired electrons in a 2p orbital
questions.hint: Compare the 2p orbital diagrams of the two atoms.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Which molecule is non-polar even though it contains polar bonds?
questions.hint: Think about whether the bond dipoles cancel because of the shape.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Explain, in terms of structure and bonding, why diamond has a much higher melting point than iodine.
questions.hint: Compare the forces that must be overcome in a giant structure and in a molecular solid.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Explain how the successive ionisation energies of an element provide evidence for the existence of electron shells.
questions.hint: Look for the large jumps and think about distance from the nucleus.

chem-sl.topic: Review: atomic structure, the mole and bonding

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Isotopes of the same element have different numbers of which particle?
questions.hint: The atomic number stays the same.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: How many neutrons are in an atom of sodium-23 (atomic number 11)?
questions.hint: Subtract the atomic number from the mass number.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: What is the electron configuration of sulfur (Z = 16)?
questions.hint: Fill sub-levels in order until 16 electrons are placed.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Lines in the visible region of the hydrogen emission spectrum come from electron transitions down to which energy level?
questions.hint: Transitions to n = 1 release more energy, in the ultraviolet.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Calculate the molar mass, in g mol⁻¹, of CaCO₃ (Ca = 40.08, C = 12.01, O = 16.00). Give your answer to 2 decimal places.
questions.hint: Remember there are three oxygen atoms.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Calculate the amount, in mol, of CaCO₃ (M = 100.09 g mol⁻¹) in 5.00 g. Give your answer to 3 significant figures.
questions.hint: Use n = m / M.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: A compound contains 40.0% carbon, 6.7% hydrogen and 53.3% oxygen by mass. What is its empirical formula?
questions.hint: Divide each percentage by the relative atomic mass, then find the simplest ratio.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Na₂CO₃ + 2HCl → 2NaCl + H₂O + CO₂. How many mol of HCl react exactly with 0.150 mol of Na₂CO₃?
questions.hint: Use the coefficients in the equation.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: The theoretical yield of a reaction is 8.00 g and the actual yield is 6.40 g. Calculate the percentage yield.
questions.hint: Divide actual by theoretical and multiply by 100.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: 50.0 cm³ of 2.00 mol dm⁻³ HCl is diluted with water to 500 cm³. Calculate the new concentration in mol dm⁻³.
questions.hint: The amount of solute does not change on dilution.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: What are the shape and bond angle of a methane (CH₄) molecule?
questions.hint: Four bonding pairs repel as far apart as possible in three dimensions.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Which intermolecular force mainly explains why water has a much higher boiling point than hydrogen sulfide?
questions.hint: Oxygen is far more electronegative than sulfur.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Name the type of bond formed when two atoms share a pair of electrons.
questions.hint: It usually forms between two non-metal atoms.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Why can solid metals conduct electricity?
questions.hint: Think about the 'sea' in the metallic bonding model.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Which substance has a giant covalent structure?
questions.hint: Look for a network of atoms joined by covalent bonds, not small molecules.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Explain, in terms of structure and bonding, why sodium chloride conducts electricity when molten but not when solid.
questions.hint: Think about whether the charged particles can move in each state.

comp-hl.topic: Review: programming fundamentals and computer systems

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which data structure works on a last in, first out (LIFO) basis?
questions.hint: Picture a pile of plates.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which binary number is equal to denary 45?
questions.hint: Use place values 32, 16, 8, 4, 2, 1.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Convert the hexadecimal number 2F to denary.
questions.hint: Each hex digit is worth 16 times the one to its right; F = 15.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: How many different values can be represented using 8 bits?
questions.hint: Each extra bit doubles the number of combinations.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: What is the output of a NOR gate when both inputs are 0? Answer 0 or 1.
questions.hint: NOR is the inverse of OR.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which CPU register holds the memory address of the next instruction to be fetched?
questions.hint: Its value increments during each fetch.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which type of primary memory is volatile?
questions.hint: Volatile means contents are lost when power is removed.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q:
Trace this algorithm and state the output.
X = 1
loop COUNT from 1 to 4
    X = X * 2
end loop
output X
questions.hint: Record X after each pass of the loop in a trace table.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q:
Trace this algorithm and state the output.
A = 10
B = 3
loop while A > B
    A = A - B
end loop
output A
questions.hint: Check the condition before every repetition.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which programming construct chooses between two paths depending on a condition?
questions.hint: Think of an if–then–else.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which statement describes a compiler?
options: It translates the whole source code into machine code before execution
It translates and executes one line at a time
It converts assembly code into high-level code
It manages memory while programs run
questions.answer: It translates the whole source code into machine code before execution
questions.hint: Consider when the translation happens.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Why does an operating system use virtual memory?
options: To use secondary storage as an extension of RAM
To speed up the network connection
questions.answer: To use secondary storage as an extension of RAM
questions.hint: It helps when RAM is full.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: In memory management, what is paging?
options: Dividing memory into fixed-size blocks that can be swapped
Printing memory contents to a file
questions.answer: Dividing memory into fixed-size blocks that can be swapped
questions.hint: Compare it with variable-sized segments.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: An array NAMES has 10 elements, indexed from 0. What is the index of the last element?
questions.hint: Indexing starts at zero.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Explain one advantage of distributing a finished program as compiled code rather than as source code to be interpreted.
questions.hint: Think about speed and what the user receives.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Describe the purpose of a trace table when testing an algorithm.
questions.hint: Consider how it records variables step by step.

comp-sl.topic: Review: programming fundamentals and computer systems

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which data structure works on a first in, first out (FIFO) basis?
questions.hint: Picture people waiting in line.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Convert denary 255 to hexadecimal.
questions.hint: 255 is the largest value one byte can hold.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: An image is 100 × 100 pixels with a colour depth of 8 bits. Calculate its size in bytes, ignoring metadata.
questions.hint: Find the number of pixels, then think about how many bytes one 8-bit pixel needs.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: What is the output of an AND gate when input A = 1 and input B = 0? Answer 0 or 1.
questions.hint: AND needs both inputs to be 1.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which logic gate outputs 1 only when its two inputs are different?
questions.hint: It is called 'exclusive'.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: What is the role of the ALU in the CPU?
options: It performs arithmetic and logical operations
It stores the next instruction address
It controls the timing of components
questions.answer: It performs arithmetic and logical operations
questions.hint: Look at the words in its full name.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which of these is secondary storage?
questions.hint: Secondary storage keeps data when the power is off.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q:
Trace this algorithm and state the output.
TOTAL = 0
loop N from 1 to 5
    if N mod 2 = 0 then
        TOTAL = TOTAL + N
    end if
end loop
output TOTAL
questions.hint: Only add N when it is even.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q:
Trace this algorithm and state the output.
COUNT = 0
NUMS = [4, 9, 2, 7, 5]
loop I from 0 to 4
    if NUMS[I] > 4 then
        COUNT = COUNT + 1
    end if
end loop
output COUNT
questions.hint: Count only the values greater than 4.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which construct repeats a block of code as long as a condition is true?
questions.hint: It is a form of iteration.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which data structure stores a fixed number of elements of the same type, accessed by an index?
questions.hint: Think of NAMES[3].

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which is a main function of an operating system?
options: Managing hardware resources such as memory and the CPU
questions.answer: Managing hardware resources such as memory and the CPU
questions.hint: It sits between the user's applications and the hardware.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: What is the name for a named value that cannot change while a program is running?
questions.hint: It is the opposite of a variable.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Explain why computers represent data in binary.
questions.hint: Think about the two states of electronic switches.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Describe two differences between RAM and ROM.
questions.hint: Consider volatility and whether the contents can be changed.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q:
Trace this algorithm and state the output.
X = 1
loop while X < 20
    X = X * 3
end loop
output X
questions.hint: Write down X after each pass and check the condition before the next one.

econ-hl.topic: Term 1 review: microeconomic foundations and market failure

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Which of the following best defines price elasticity of demand (PED)?
options: The responsiveness of quantity demanded to a change in price
The responsiveness of price to a change in demand
The change in total revenue when price changes
The responsiveness of supply to a change in price
questions.answer: The responsiveness of quantity demanded to a change in price
questions.hint: Think about which variable reacts and which causes the change.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: The price of a good rises from $10 to $12 and quantity demanded falls from 100 to 90 units. Calculate the PED (give the absolute value to 1 decimal place).
questions.hint: Use percentage change in quantity divided by percentage change in price.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: If PED for a product is 0.3, what happens to a firm's total revenue when it raises the price?
questions.hint: Demand is inelastic, so quantity falls proportionally less than price rises.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: A good with a negative income elasticity of demand (YED) is called what type of good?
questions.hint: Think about what happens to demand when incomes rise.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Cross elasticity of demand (XED) between two goods is +1.8. The goods are:
questions.hint: A positive sign means the price of one and the demand for the other move in the same direction.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: On a diagram showing a specific (per-unit) indirect tax, how does the supply curve shift?
options: Parallel shift upwards by the amount of the tax
Shifts downwards by the amount of the tax
questions.answer: Parallel shift upwards by the amount of the tax
questions.hint: A specific tax adds the same amount to the cost of every unit.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: When demand is price inelastic, who bears most of the incidence of an indirect tax?
questions.hint: The less responsive side of the market cannot avoid the tax easily.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: A maximum price set below the equilibrium price is most likely to lead to:
questions.hint: Compare quantity demanded and quantity supplied at the lower price.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Which statement about a minimum price (price floor) for agricultural goods is correct?
options: It creates a surplus the government may have to buy
It creates a shortage of the product
questions.answer: It creates a surplus the government may have to buy
questions.hint: Above equilibrium, producers want to sell more than consumers want to buy.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: What term describes the situation where the free market fails to achieve allocative efficiency?
questions.hint: It is the theme of the second half of the microeconomics unit.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: In a diagram of a negative production externality, which curve lies above the marginal private cost (MPC) curve?
questions.hint: The external cost is added to the private cost.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Education is often given as an example of which type of externality?
questions.hint: Think about who benefits when someone else becomes educated.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Which characteristic makes a good 'non-excludable'?
options: People who do not pay cannot be prevented from using it
Use by one person reduces availability for others
It is provided only by private firms
Its price is set by the government
questions.answer: People who do not pay cannot be prevented from using it
questions.hint: This is the property that causes the free-rider problem.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Explain, using the concept of welfare loss, why a subsidy on a good with positive consumption externalities can improve allocative efficiency.
questions.hint: Mention where the market produces compared with the socially optimal output and what happens to the welfare loss triangle.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Evaluate the use of carbon taxes as a method of reducing negative production externalities.
questions.hint: Weigh up advantages (internalising the externality, revenue) against problems (measuring the external cost, inelastic demand, competitiveness).

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Explain two common errors students make when labelling diagrams in Paper 1 answers, and how to avoid them.
questions.hint: Think about axes, curve labels, equilibrium points and shading of areas.

econ-sl.topic: Term 1 review: microeconomic foundations and market failure

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: What does the law of demand state, ceteris paribus?
options: As price rises, quantity demanded falls
As price rises, quantity demanded rises
questions.answer: As price rises, quantity demanded falls
questions.hint: It describes the slope of the demand curve.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Which of these causes a movement along the demand curve rather than a shift?
options: A change in the good's own price
A change in the price of a substitute
questions.answer: A change in the good's own price
questions.hint: Only one factor is on the axes of the diagram.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Quantity demanded rises by 20% when price falls by 10%. Calculate the PED (absolute value).
questions.hint: Divide the percentage change in quantity by the percentage change in price.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: A PED value of 2 means demand is:
questions.hint: Compare the value with 1.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Which factor makes demand for a good more price inelastic?
options: It takes up a large share of income
A long time period to adjust
questions.hint: If consumers cannot switch easily, they keep buying.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: What term is used for the difference between what consumers are willing to pay and what they actually pay?
questions.hint: It is shown as an area under the demand curve and above the price.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: If price elasticity of supply (PES) is 0, the supply curve is:
questions.hint: Quantity supplied does not respond at all to price.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Which government intervention shifts the supply curve to the right?
questions.hint: It lowers producers' costs.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Rent controls in a city are an example of:
questions.hint: Rent controls stop landlords charging above a certain level.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: A minimum wage set above the equilibrium wage is likely to cause:
questions.hint: More people want to work at the higher wage than firms want to hire.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Smoke from a factory harming nearby residents is an example of:
questions.hint: A third party is harmed when the good is produced.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: What name is given to people who use a public good without paying for it?
questions.hint: Think of someone getting a ride without buying a ticket.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Which of these is the best example of a public good?
questions.hint: Look for a good that is non-rival and non-excludable.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: In a Paper 1 answer, what is the main purpose of a real-world example?
questions.hint: Examiners reward applying theory to actual situations.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Using a diagram description, explain how an indirect tax on sugary drinks affects price, quantity and government revenue.
questions.hint: Describe the supply shift, the new equilibrium and the rectangle that represents tax revenue.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Evaluate the use of a maximum price on a basic food product.
questions.hint: Consider who gains, who loses, and possible shortages or black markets.

en-hl.topic: Term 1 review: non-literary analysis and first works

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which term describes repeating a word or phrase at the beginning of successive clauses?
questions.hint: The repetition comes at the start, not the end.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: In a speech, a question asked for effect rather than to get an answer is called:
questions.hint: The speaker expects the audience to know the answer already.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: In visual texts, which term describes the angle where the camera looks up at a subject, often making it seem powerful?
questions.hint: Where is the camera placed relative to the subject?

questions.subject: en
questions.q: In an advertisement, the arrangement of elements that guides where the viewer looks first is called:
questions.hint: It is about which element stands out most.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Persepolis is best described as which kind of text?
questions.hint: It combines images with the narrator's account of her own childhood.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What historical event is the background to the opening chapters of Persepolis?
options: The fall of the Berlin Wall
questions.hint: The story begins in Tehran around 1979–1980.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: The panels of Persepolis are drawn mainly in:
questions.hint: Think about the stark visual style of the book.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: In The Handmaid's Tale, what is the name of the regime that rules the former United States?
questions.hint: It takes its name from a biblical place.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: In The Handmaid's Tale, what is the narrator's name in the household of the Commander?
questions.hint: Her name shows who she 'belongs' to.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: The Handmaid's Tale is narrated mainly in which way?
options: First person, with shifts between present and past
questions.answer: First person, with shifts between present and past
questions.hint: Whose voice do we hear, and does she remember the time before?

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which feature of The Handmaid's Tale's ending makes readers question the reliability of the story?
options: The Historical Notes from a future academic conference
questions.answer: The Historical Notes from a future academic conference
questions.hint: The final section is set long after the events of the novel.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which global issue links Persepolis and The Handmaid's Tale most clearly?
options: Control of individual freedom and the body by the state
questions.answer: Control of individual freedom and the body by the state
questions.hint: Think about rules imposed on women in both works.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: In Paper 1, how can you move from identifying a technique to analysing its effect? Give an example sentence structure.
questions.hint: Use a pattern like technique + evidence + effect on the reader + link to purpose.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Explain how the use of a child's perspective in Persepolis shapes the reader's understanding of political events.
questions.hint: Think about simplicity, irony, and what the young narrator does not fully understand.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Write a topic sentence for a Paper 1 paragraph analysing how an advertisement uses imagery and slogan together to persuade.
questions.hint: Name the technique, the effect and the purpose in one clear claim.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which of Aristotle's three appeals relies on the speaker's credibility?
questions.hint: The other two appeal to emotion and to logic.

en-sl.topic: Term 1 review: non-literary analysis and first works

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What is the 'purpose' of a text in non-literary analysis?
options: What the writer wants to achieve
Who the text is written for
questions.answer: What the writer wants to achieve
questions.hint: For example, to persuade, inform or entertain.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which term means the intended readers or viewers of a text?
questions.hint: Ask yourself: who is this for?

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Placing two contrasting ideas side by side in balanced phrases is called:
questions.hint: An example: 'not a burden, but a gift'.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which appeal is being used when a charity advert shows a sad image to make viewers feel sympathy?
questions.hint: Which appeal targets the emotions?

questions.subject: en
questions.q: In a print advertisement, text that explains or fixes the meaning of an image is called:
questions.hint: It 'anchors' the image to one meaning.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Using 'we' and 'us' in a speech mainly creates:
options: A sense of unity with the audience
questions.answer: A sense of unity with the audience
questions.hint: Inclusive pronouns bring the speaker and audience together.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which term describes the level of formality in a text?
questions.hint: It can be formal, informal or colloquial.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: In Persepolis, the narrator tells the story of:
questions.hint: It is a memoir.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: In Persepolis, what are girls required to wear at school after the revolution, as shown at the start of the book?
questions.hint: The first chapter is named after it.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Near the end of the first part of Persepolis, the young narrator is sent to study in which country?
questions.hint: She goes to Vienna.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: In The Handmaid's Tale, what colour do the Handmaids wear?
questions.hint: Think of the colour linked to their role and the cover image.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: In The Handmaid's Tale, who is Moira?
options: An Aunt at the Red Center
questions.hint: She represents resistance and escape.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What kind of novel is The Handmaid's Tale?
questions.hint: It imagines a frightening society.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Write one analytical sentence about the effect of a rhetorical question in a persuasive speech.
questions.hint: Name the technique and explain how it makes the audience think or feel.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Explain one way the visual style of Persepolis supports its themes.
questions.hint: Think about simplicity, contrast and how violence is drawn.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Why is it important to refer to the guiding question in a Paper 1 paragraph?
questions.hint: Think about focus, relevance and the assessment criteria.

en_lit-hl.topic: Term 1 review: poetry, prose and drama

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: A fourteen-line poem written in iambic pentameter is usually called a:
questions.hint: Count the lines.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: The turn in thought or argument in a poem, often in a sonnet, is called the:
questions.hint: It comes from the Italian word for 'turn'.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: A pause in the middle of a line of poetry, often marked by punctuation, is called:
questions.hint: It breaks the line inside, not at the end.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: When a sentence runs over from one line of poetry into the next without punctuation, this is called:
questions.hint: The meaning spills over the line break.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: A narrator whose account the reader cannot fully trust is called:
questions.hint: Think about bias, limited knowledge or self-deception.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: Free indirect discourse is a technique where:
options: A third-person narrator takes on a character's thoughts and voice
Characters speak directly to the audience
The story is told in letters
questions.answer: A third-person narrator takes on a character's thoughts and voice
questions.hint: It blends narration and inner thought.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: When the audience knows something a character on stage does not, this is called:
questions.hint: It creates tension in drama.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: What is the term for a long speech in a play where a character, alone on stage, reveals their thoughts?
questions.hint: It is spoken alone, not to another character.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: Written instructions in a play script about movement, setting or tone are called:
questions.hint: They are usually printed in italics.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: Hints in a text about events that will happen later are called:
questions.hint: They prepare the reader for what is coming.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: In the IB Paper 1 for Literature, what are you asked to write about?
options: An unseen literary passage, guided by a question
A comparison of two studied works
questions.answer: An unseen literary passage, guided by a question
questions.hint: You have not studied the extract before the exam.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: Which assessment criterion focuses on how well you explain the writer's choices and their effects?
questions.hint: It is about 'how' and 'why', not just 'what'.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: Explain how enjambment can affect the pace and meaning of a poem.
questions.hint: Think about how the reader moves between lines and what is emphasised.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: Choose a technique common in drama and explain how it can create tension for an audience.
questions.hint: Consider dramatic irony, asides, stage directions or silence.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: Write a strong opening sentence for a Paper 1 essay that states a clear interpretation of an unseen poem about loss.
questions.hint: Your claim should mention both meaning and method.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: Evaluate whether a first-person narrator makes a prose work more or less convincing for the reader.
questions.hint: Weigh intimacy and voice against limited perspective and bias.

en_lit-sl.topic: Term 1 review: poetry, prose and drama

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: A comparison using 'like' or 'as' is called a:
questions.hint: Look for the comparison word.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: Giving human qualities to something non-human is called:
questions.hint: The word 'person' is inside it.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: The repetition of vowel sounds in nearby words is called:
questions.hint: Vowels are a, e, i, o, u.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: A group of lines forming a unit in a poem is called a:
questions.hint: It is the poetry equivalent of a paragraph.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: The overall feeling or atmosphere of a text is called its:
questions.hint: It is what the reader feels while reading.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: A scene that interrupts the story to show earlier events is called a:
questions.hint: It goes back in time.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: In prose fiction, the main character is often called the:
questions.hint: The 'pro' character drives the story.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: A character who contrasts with another to highlight their qualities is called a:
questions.hint: Think of something that makes a jewel shine brighter.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: What is the term for a short comment made by a character to the audience that other characters on stage cannot hear?
questions.hint: It is spoken 'to the side'.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: Which of these is a feature of drama but not usually of prose?
questions.hint: Think about what a director and actors need.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: In Paper 1, what should every body paragraph include?
options: A claim, evidence from the text and analysis of effect
questions.answer: A claim, evidence from the text and analysis of effect
questions.hint: Examiners reward analysis, not retelling.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: Explain how a symbol can develop the theme of a prose work. Use an invented example if you wish.
questions.hint: Say what the object is, what it represents and how it changes or recurs.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: Explain one difference between how a poem and a play can show a character's emotions.
questions.hint: Consider imagery and voice in poetry against actions, dialogue and staging in drama.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: How can you use the assessment criteria to check your own Paper 1 paragraph?
questions.hint: Think about analysis, focus, organisation and language.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: Why is it more effective to embed short quotations rather than copy long ones?
questions.hint: Think about precision and the space left for analysis.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: The writer's attitude towards the subject is called the:
questions.hint: It can be described as bitter, playful, admiring or ironic.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Choose the correct auxiliary: « Hier, je ___ allée au marché. »
questions.hint: Aller is one of the verbs that take être.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Choose the correct past participle: « Nous avons ___ un film. » (voir)
questions.hint: The past participle of voir is irregular.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Write the passé composé of 'je prends' (prendre).
questions.hint: Prendre has an irregular past participle.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Which tense is used for a background description in the past, e.g. « Il ___ beau »?
questions.hint: Descriptions and weather in the past usually use the imperfect.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Complete with the correct tenses: « Je ___ la télé quand le téléphone ___. »
questions.hint: An ongoing action is interrupted by a completed one.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Choose the correct agreement: « Elles sont ___ hier soir. » (partir)
questions.hint: With être, the participle agrees with a feminine plural subject.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Which word means 'heritage' in French, often used in the theme Identities?
questions.hint: It is linked to culture passed down through generations.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: What does « s'intégrer » mean?
questions.hint: Think of the English word that looks similar.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Which phrase means 'I feel torn between two cultures'?
options: Je me sens partagé entre deux cultures
Je me sens perdu dans la ville
questions.answer: Je me sens partagé entre deux cultures
questions.hint: 'Partagé' here means divided.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Translate into French: 'a gap year'.
questions.hint: It is a year taken off, often to travel or work.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Choose the correct pluperfect: « Quand je suis arrivé, le train ___. »
questions.hint: The action happened before another past action.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Which verb is NOT conjugated with être in the passé composé?
questions.hint: Think of the 'house of être' verbs of movement and change of state.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Choose the correct sentence: 'We went abroad last summer.'
options: Nous sommes partis à l'étranger l'été dernier.
Nous avons partis à l'étranger l'été dernier.
Nous partions à l'étranger l'été dernier.
Nous sommes parti à l'étranger l'été dernier.
questions.answer: Nous sommes partis à l'étranger l'été dernier.
questions.hint: Partir takes être, and the participle agrees with the subject.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Write 3–4 sentences in French describing a memorable trip, using both the passé composé and the imparfait.
questions.hint: Use the imperfect for description and the passé composé for completed events.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: In French, give your opinion in 3–4 sentences: Is it important to keep your native language when you live in another country? Justify your answer.
questions.hint: Use connectors like 'd'abord', 'de plus', 'cependant'.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Write a short blog entry (4–5 sentences in French) about a festival or tradition that is part of your identity.
questions.hint: Include what you do, why it matters, and a past memory.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Choose the correct auxiliary: « Il ___ mangé une pizza. »
questions.hint: Most verbs use avoir in the passé composé.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Choose the correct past participle: « J'ai ___ mes devoirs. » (finir)
questions.hint: -ir verbs often end in -i.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Write the passé composé of 'tu fais' (faire).
questions.hint: Faire has an irregular past participle.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Choose the correct form: « Elle ___ arrivée à huit heures. »
questions.hint: Arriver is a verb of movement.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Which tense is used for a habit in the past: « Quand j'étais petit, je ___ au parc tous les jours »?
questions.hint: Repeated past actions use the imperfect.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Write the imparfait of 'nous avons' (avoir).
questions.hint: Imperfect endings: -ais, -ais, -ait, -ions, -iez, -aient.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: What does « les origines » mean?
questions.hint: It looks like the English word.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Which word means 'customs' or 'traditions'?
questions.hint: Be careful with false friends.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Which phrase means 'I was born in…'?
questions.hint: Naître uses être in the passé composé.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: What does « un séjour » mean?
questions.hint: You might spend a 'séjour' in another country.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Translate into French: 'the youth hostel'.
questions.hint: It's a cheap place for young travellers to stay.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Complete: « Pendant les vacances, nous ___ (visiter) un château. »
questions.hint: A single completed action in the past.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Which connector means 'however'?
questions.hint: It introduces a contrast.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Write 3 sentences in French about what you did last weekend, using the passé composé.
questions.hint: Include where you went, with whom and one opinion.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Write 3–4 sentences in French describing yourself and your family background.
questions.hint: Mention nationality, languages and one tradition.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Write 3–4 sentences in French about a holiday when you were younger, using the imparfait for description.
questions.hint: Describe the weather, the place and how you felt.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: In the demographic transition model, which stage has high birth rates and falling death rates?
questions.hint: This is when the population grows fastest.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: A population pyramid with a wide base and narrow top typically shows:
options: High birth rates and a young population
questions.answer: High birth rates and a young population
questions.hint: Look at the size of the youngest age groups.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: A country has 30 million people aged 0–14, 10 million aged 65+, and 60 million aged 15–64. Calculate the dependency ratio.
questions.hint: Divide the dependent population by the working-age population and multiply by 100; round to 1 decimal place.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: What is the term for the number of births per 1,000 people per year?
questions.hint: It is 'crude' because it does not account for age structure.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Which term describes the movement of people from rural to urban areas?
questions.hint: The proportion living in towns and cities increases.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: A forced migrant who has crossed an international border to escape persecution is called a:
questions.hint: An internally displaced person has not crossed a border.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Which gas is the largest contributor to the enhanced greenhouse effect from human activity?
questions.hint: It comes mainly from burning fossil fuels.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Which of the following is a natural carbon sink?
questions.hint: A sink absorbs more carbon than it releases.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Reducing greenhouse gas emissions is a strategy of climate change:
questions.hint: Adaptation means adjusting to impacts instead.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Building higher sea walls in coastal cities is an example of climate change:
questions.hint: It deals with the effects rather than the causes.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Which term describes the sensitivity of the climate to positive feedback, e.g. melting ice reducing albedo?
questions.hint: The change makes itself stronger.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Which resource issue is linked to the idea of 'peak oil'?
options: The point when oil production reaches its maximum and then declines
The highest price oil has ever reached
questions.answer: The point when oil production reaches its maximum and then declines
questions.hint: Think about production over time.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Water stress is usually defined as having annual water supplies below how much per person?
questions.hint: Below 1,000 is called scarcity.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Describe the pattern shown by a population pyramid of an ageing country and suggest two challenges this creates.
questions.hint: Look at the shape of the top and base, then think about pensions and healthcare.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Using a case study, explain one strategy used to manage a country's population change.
questions.hint: Name the place, the policy and one outcome.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Evaluate the view that adaptation is more important than mitigation for low-income countries facing climate change.
questions.hint: Weigh up costs, urgency and responsibility for emissions.
